hypothesis: The measured AVX2 candidates do not isolate mapping cost: the valid single-block candidate averaged 22.43 µs and a paired-loop candidate 17.93 µs. This experiment tests whether forming one per-byte arithmetic offset from the existing mutually exclusive range masks, then adding it to the input vector, is faster than separate class-specific arithmetic mappings. The combined offset may reduce mapping instructions but add dependency depth; short inputs and tails should remain unaffected.
notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed. The candidate retains runtime AVX2 detection, the AVX2 target attribute, bounded 32-byte loads and 24-byte output, and scalar quartet/padding fallback; no build flags or thread settings are changed. Moving <cstring> before the decoder also fixes the recorded compilation diagnostic where std::memcpy was used before its declaration. No local build, correctness checks, Lena test, or timing were run; the controller should validate empty/short inputs, block boundaries, padding, random valid strings, and Lena before repeated native timing. The supplied target is EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2, but frozen ISA flags were not independently inspected.
transformations: Moved standard headers, including <cstring>, before their first use to address the known build diagnostic.

Replaced separate class-specific sextet arithmetic with per-class arithmetic offsets combined under the existing AVX2 range masks, followed by one vector byte addition; retained vector packing and all scalar, tail, padding, dispatch, and bounded memory paths.
